reading.body:
CyrusOne's Allen campus holds 77 MW of IT capacity, second among the 19 Texas data centers with published power figures, but its compliance certifications narrow its fit for large-scale AI training.

The three facilities, DFW3, DFW4, and DFW5, span 976,000 square feet in Dallas-Fort Worth, a metro with established power and fiber but not among the largest AI cluster regions published to date. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 77 MW represents roughly 1,900 racks of compute. The certifications, HIPAA, FISMA, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, and SSAE 16 Type II, target regulated workloads that have no standard requirement for AI training, so the campus is less directly addressable for frontier compute. Green Globes certification indicates attention to energy efficiency, a secondary concern when power is the binding constraint.

Texas publishes capacity for fewer than one in seven of its 133 data center sites, so the 475 MW state total is a floor, not a full measure. The suitability score of 76 reflects published IT capacity and operator type, but it is missing announced expansion, the key unknown for whether this campus can grow into AI scale. The data does not state any repurposing or expansion plan.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
